'''Israel Pecht''' (Hebrew: '''ישראל פכט'''; born June 28, 1937) is an [[Israelis|Israeli]] [[Physical chemistry|physical chemist]] and Professor Emeritus at the Faculty of Biology at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]]. He is a former Chair of the Academic Board of the [[Israel Science Foundation]] and served as President of the [[International Union for Pure and Applied Biophysics]]. His research is in the study of physicochemical processes in living organisms.

== Biography ==

=== Early life ===
Israel Pecht was born in [[Vienna]], the son of Yocheved Eva (née Preminger)<ref>{{Cite web |title=אווה יוכבד פכט |url=https://www.geni.com/people/Eva-Pecht/6000000007351373690 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=geni.com}}</ref> and Benjamin Isaac (Benno) Pächt.<ref>{{Cite web |title=בנימין יצחק פכט |url=https://www.geni.com/people/Benjamin-Itzhak-Pecht/6000000007787080938 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=geni.com}}</ref> He was named after his maternal grandfather. Israel and his parents immigrated to [[Mandatory Palestine]] after the [[Anschluss]], in late 1938. Many of his relatives perished in the Holocaust. He grew up in the [[Old North, Tel Aviv|Old North]] of [[Tel Aviv]].

He served in the IDF in the Field Security Unit of the Southern Command and did most of his reserve duty in [[Lebanon]] with the [[IDF Spokesperson's Unit|IDF Spokesperson’s Unit]]. After his discharge in 1958, he began his studies towards master's degree in chemistry at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], completing it in 1962. His thesis work was carried out at the Isotope Research Department of the Weizmann Institute, where he continued with his doctoral studies under the supervision of Prof. Michael Anbar.''<ref name=":2" />'' His Ph.D. dissertation, submitted in 1967, was titled ''“Redox Processes Between Transition Metal Ions and their Ligands.”<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=תהליכי חימצון-חיזור בין יוני מתכות מעבר לבין ליגנדים |url=https://weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/discovery/delivery/972WIS_INST:972WIS_V1/1229668840003596 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com}}</ref>'' During his doctoral studies, Pecht was one of four instructors at the first summer science camp for youth at the Weizmann Institute, alongside Moshe Rishpon, Alpha Peled, and Gideon Zwas.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Davidson Institute of Science Education |url=https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=606407566076895&id=107114862672837&set=p.606407566076895&locale=he_IL |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=facebook.com}}</ref>

=== Independent research career ===
Upon completing his PhD, Pecht traveled to [[Göttingen]], [[West Germany]], where he conducted postdoctoral research at the [[Max Planck Society|Max Planck Institute]] for Physical Chemistry under Prof. [[Manfred Eigen]] (Nobel Laureate 1967).<ref name=":12" /> He was the first Israeli to carry out scientific postdoctoral research in Germany after World War II.<ref name=":02">{{Cite book |url=https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/sites/default/files/images/Books/The%20Graduates.pdf |title=The Graduates}}</ref> Upon returning to Israel in 1970, he was appointed a researcher in the Department of Chemical Immunology at the Weizmann Institute.<ref>{{Cite web |title=אולפנת קיץ תיפתח מחר במכון ויצמן |url=https://www.nli.org.il/he/newspapers/mar/1970/07/26/01/article/60 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=nli.org.il |language=he}}</ref> In 1978, he was appointed Associate Professor<ref>{{Cite web |title=⁨העלאות בדרגה במכון ויצמן |url=https://www.nli.org.il/he/newspapers/mar/1978/01/23/01/article/233 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=nli.org.il |language=he}}</ref> and, in 1984, Full Professor.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: CV |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Pecht_Israel/CV |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=ae-info.org}}</ref> He officially retired in 2006 but continued conducting active research.

Over the years, Pecht was invited to conduct research at institutions such as the [[University of Konstanz]], [[Max Planck Institute for Biophysical Chemistry]] in Göttingen, [[Stanford University]], the [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech), [[Paris Diderot University|Paris VII University]], and the [[Pasteur Institute|Pasteur]] and [[Curie Institute (Paris)|Curie Institutes]].<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: CV |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Pecht_Israel/CV |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=ae-info.org}}</ref>

=== Academic and organizational roles ===
In 1974, Pecht was appointed head of the Department of Biological Services at the Weizmann Institute.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ד"ר ישראל פכט, מהמחלקה לאימונולוגיה כימית, מונה לאחראי על השרותים הביולוגיים |url=https://weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/discovery/delivery/972WIS_INST:972WIS_V1/1240050370003596 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com}}</ref> In the mid-1970s, he served on the Chemistry and Biology teaching committees of the Feinberg Graduate School and headed the [[Charles Clore]] Scholars Program in the 1980s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=הפרס ע"ש קלור הוענק למחלקה להוראת המדעים |url=https://weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/discovery/delivery/972WIS_INST:972WIS_V1/1240049530003596 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com}}</ref> In 1981, together with Prof. Ruth Arnon, he organized the Rothschild Workshop on Biophysical Aspects of Immunology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=חידושים בתחום החיסון - באולפנת רוטשילד |url=https://weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/discovery/delivery/972WIS_INST:972WIS_V1/1245106910003596 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com}}</ref> In 1985, he founded the Minerva Center for Biomembranes Research, which he headed until 1994. He served as Head of the Department of Chemical Immunology from 1989 to 1992<ref>{{Cite web |title=מינויים חדשים בסגל המדעי של המכון |url=https://weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/discovery/delivery/972WIS_INST:972WIS_V1/1240049510003596 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com}}</ref> and again from 1998 to 2002 (by then, renamed the Department of Immunology).

From 1986 to 1991, Pecht served as President of the Israel Society for Biochemistry. From 1989 to 1995, he was Chairman of the Academic Board of the Israel Science Foundation, having previously chaired its Division of Natural Sciences. Pecht held senior positions in international organizations: Vice President (1992–1995) and President (1995–1998) of the European Federation of Immunological Societies (EFIS); Vice President (1996–1999) and President (1999–2002) of the International Union for Pure and Applied Biophysics (IUPAB); and Secretary General (2006–2016) of the [[Federation of European Biochemical Societies]] (FEBS), where he is now an Honorary Executive Committee Member. He has also served as a consultant to [[UNESCO]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Israel Pecht {{!}} ScienceBlog |url=https://scienceblog.at/israel-pecht |access-date=2026-08-15 |website=scienceblog.at}}</ref> the Max Planck Society, and other academic bodies in West Germany and France, as well as to the Chief Scientist of [[Ministry of Health (Israel)|Israel’s Ministry of Health]].

Since 2024, a prestigious annual award named after Pecht has been granted by FEBS.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-26 |title=The Israel Pecht Award 2024 - FEBS |work=FEBS |url=https://www.febs.org/news/the-israel-pecht-award-2024-febs-recognition-award-for-outstanding-contribution-to-the-molecular-biosciences-community/ |access-date=2025-07-21}}</ref>

== Research ==
Over his career, Pecht published around 550 papers and supervised dozens of graduate students, including Prof. Jakub Abramson<ref>{{Cite web |title=Examination of functional role(s) of the mast cell function-associated antigen (MAFA) |url=https://weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/discovery/fulldisplay?docid=alma990001412780203596&context=L&vid=972WIS_INST:972WIS_V1&lang=en&search_scope=All_Institution_and_CentralIndex&adaptor=Local%20Search%20Engine&tab=Everything&query=any,contains,%D7%99%D7%A9%D7%A8%D7%90%D7%9C%20%D7%A4%D7%9B%D7%98&offset=0&pcAvailability=true |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com}}</ref> and Prof. Doron Lancet<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kinetic and thermodynamic studies of hapten induced conformational changes in immunoglobulins |url=https://weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/discovery/delivery/972WIS_INST:972WIS_V1/1229661040003596 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com}}</ref> of the Weizmann Institute, as well as Dr. David Haselkorn,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kinetic and spectroscopic analysis of an antibody binding site |url=https://weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/discovery/fulldisplay?docid=alma993559984603596&context=L&vid=972WIS_INST:972WIS_V1&lang=en&search_scope=All_Institution_and_CentralIndex&adaptor=Local%20Search%20Engine&tab=Everything&query=any,contains,%D7%99%D7%A9%D7%A8%D7%90%D7%9C%20%D7%A4%D7%9B%D7%98&offset=0&pcAvailability=true |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com}}</ref> former CEO of Clal Biotechnology. He served as editor of the journal ''[[Immunology Letters]]'' and contributed editorial work to many other journals in his field.

Pecht’s research focuses on elucidating physicochemical principles underlying biochemical processes, by identifying and characterizing their elementary steps. For example those of transmembrane signaling processes that regulate immune cell activity. His lab became a global center for the biophysical study of molecular processes in immunology, pioneering analysis of antigen interactions of monoclonal antibodies using thermodynamic and kinetic methods. These methods were later applied to the study of conformational changes in [[T cell|T-cell]] receptors upon binding to target antigens presented on cell membranes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-11-23 |title=התאמה מאולצת - מסע הקסם המדעי - חדשות מדע, תגליות ומידע לציבור |url=https://heb.wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/life-sciences/n-3967 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=מסע הקסם המדעי - חדשות מדע, תגליות ומידע לציבור מבית מכון ויצמן למדע |language=he}}</ref>

As a model system, Pecht and his group investigated the activation cascade of mast cells, from the binding of IgE antibodies to their specific cell-surface receptors, through the coupling processes of cell activation, leading finally to the mediators’ secretion response.<ref name=":1" />

In parallel, his lab studied electron transfer processes within and between protein molecules and pioneered the use of pulse-radiation to resolve the mechanisms of reactions in key [[redox]] [[Enzyme|enzymes]], such as [[Cytochrome c oxidase|cytochrome-c oxidase]].<ref name=":12" />

In recent years, Pecht has collaborated with Prof. Mudi Sheves and Prof. David Cahen on research aimed at understanding the mechanism of electrical conduction in proteins.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-09-05 |title=חלבונים, קוונטים וזרמים חשמליים - מסע הקסם המדעי - חדשות מדע, תגליות ומידע לציבור |url=https://heb.wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/chemistry/n-7690 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=מסע הקסם המדעי - חדשות מדע, תגליות ומידע לציבור מבית מכון ויצמן למדע |language=he}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
* Member, European Molecular Biology Organization (EMBO) (1977)
* Jacques Mimran Chair in Chemical Immunology (1980–1992)
* Honorary Member, Swedish Biophysical Society (1980)
* Fairchild Distinguished Visiting Professor, Caltech (1981–1982)
* Schwerin Research Award (1984)
* H. Dudley Wright Achievement Award (1986)
* Morton and Anne Kleiman Chair in Chemical Immunology (1993–2006)
* Henri de Rothschild Fellowship, Curie Institute (1995)
* Honorary Member, Hungarian Society for Immunology (1997)
* Federal Republic of Germany Cross of Merit (1998)
* Honorary Doctorate, Faculty of Medicine, University of Debrecen, Hungary (1999)
* Landau Prize for Life Sciences (2003)
* Honorary Member, Hungarian Academy of Sciences (2007)
* Honorary Member, Spanish Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (SEBBM) (2012)
* Honorary Doctorate, National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (2013)
* Member, Academia Europaea (2016)
* Medal marking the centennial of the Nencki Institute, Polish Academy of Sciences (2017)
* Gold Medal of Charles University in Prague for achievements in biochemistry and immunology (2017)
* Honorary Member, Polish Biochemical Society (2018)

== Personal life ==
Since 1962, Pecht has been married to Dr. Marit Pecht (née Landau), a biochemist who worked for many years at the Weizmann Institute.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |url=https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/sites/default/files/images/Books/The%20Graduates.pdf |title=The Graduates}}</ref> They had two children, Galit (deceased) and Yuval. He resides in Rehovot.
